tob-10043: Israel Abrahams, a noted Jewish scholar, gathers here his essays and translations on Jewish literature and history. The title essay presents ‘The Book of Delight,’ a medieval Hebrew work of wit and wisdom, in English for the first time for many readers. The remaining papers touch on Jewish life, letters, and learning across the centuries, opening a little-known corner of world literature.
tob-13643: Presented as the distilled wisdom of Hermes Trismegistus, the thrice-great sage of Egypt, The Kybalion lays out seven universal laws — including the law of attraction’s ancestor, the principle of vibration. The Three Initiates wrote it for the early twentieth-century seeker, packaging ancient-seeming doctrine in crisp modern prose. It endures as a gateway text of the occult revival.
tob-4043: Poet and playwright Friedrich Schiller turned thinker in these essays on beauty, art, and human freedom. He holds that the play of beauty can make us whole, joining our feeling side to our reasoning side. Set down in the 1790s, these essays steered German views of art and schooling for a hundred years.
tob-4243: Lady Charlotte Guest’s Mabinogion bears the Welsh wonder-tales into English — Pwyll’s otherworld ride, Bran’s doomed sailing, the spells of Math and Gwydion. Her 1849 rendering, bettered in 1877, was a milestone of Celtic learning. The tales shine with a strangeness no later hand has dulled.
tob-10543: Macauliffe’s Religion of the Sikhs is the classic English account of Sikhism — the lives of the ten Gurus and the teachings of the Granth Sahib. His six-volume work introduced the faith to the Western world. The book remains the foundational English Sikh history.
tob-13143: Swami Vivekananda’s Karma Yoga teaches the path of selfless work — freedom through action without clinging to results. His Chicago lectures made the Gita’s teaching practical for modern readers. Work becomes worship when the ego steps aside. The book remains a beloved introduction to yoga’s active path.
tob-14243: The Rising-Treatise — Nag Hammadi’s first book, fourth tract — is the Gnostic letter on rising from the dead, in Barnstone and Peel’s Englishing. Its love-teaching mingles Paul and Gnosis. The text is a jewel of the Nag Hammadi hoard.
tob-0043: The CIA Programs and Mind Control book collection gathers works on MKULTRA and related secret programs. The volumes document the agency’s drug and hypnosis experiments on unwitting subjects. The Church Committee exposed it all. The collection is a disturbing primary archive.
arxiv-2605-08843: Simulating physics on a computer means chopping continuous reality into discrete chunks, and the training objective has to respect that chopping. Yuan Mei, Xingyu Song, Xiaowen Song, and Naoya Takeishi reframe the training measures used for discretized physical simulations. The 2026 paper is about making machine-learned simulators honest about their own discretization.
arxiv-2605-09043: Words drift in emotional meaning — what freedom feels like shifts over time — and sometimes the drift snaps like a phase transition. Napassorn Litchiowong studies affective meaning divergence, hunting the hidden drift that precedes the break. The 2026 paper is computational linguistics on how the feelings attached to words change.
arxiv-2605-09343: Vision-language-action models fumble scenes they do not understand structurally. Zeyu Li and Lei Li give them scene knowledge graph priors — SKG-VLA — for structured semantics and multimodal reasoning for decision making. The 2026 paper grounds robot perception in explicit scene knowledge.
arxiv-2605-09243: Brain recordings — fMRI, EEG — are expensive to collect, so their value for machine learning needs quantifying. Lane Lewis and Zhixin Wang ask how much brain data is actually worth for ML. The 2026 paper is a cost-benefit analysis for neuro-AI.
arxiv-2605-09543: Modeling starlight without assuming local thermodynamic equilibrium — non-LTE — is accurate and agonizingly slow in 3D. A. Vicente Arévalo, A. Asensio Ramos, and C. J. Díaz Baso accelerate the synthesis with graph neural networks. The 2026 paper is solar physics at machine speed.
arxiv-2605-10043: Personalizing LLMs from binary feedback — thumbs up, thumbs down — with preference-corrected optimization. Xilai Ma, Liye Zhao, Weijun Yao, and colleagues build the framework. The 2026 paper is personalization from the simplest possible signal. It learns rich preferences from binary choices.
arxiv-2605-10143: Thompson's groups and Teichmüller modular groups acting on generalized Cantor sets — infinite symmetry on fractal dust. Hiroshige Shiga explores the deep connection. The 2026 paper is geometric group theory on fractals. It groups the Cantor dust with Teichmüller precision.
arxiv-2605-10243: Electroweak physics and long-lived particles at LHCb — the LHC's forward eye on exotic decays. Felicia Volle presents on behalf of the LHCb Collaboration. The 2026 paper is particle physics. It hunts exotic long-lived particles carefully at the LHCb experiment.
arxiv-2605-10643: A single-layer model doing language modeling — can one layer really suffice? Zanmin Wang demonstrates that it can. The 2026 paper is LLM architecture minimalism. It proves a single layer can model language. One layer is enough. Language modeling, minimized. Simplicity triumphs.
pmc-13455643: Long COVID fatigue — improved by VSL#3 probiotic supplementation, according to the DELong#3 randomized placebo-controlled trial. pmc-13549343: Undulator radiation at the Hefei Advanced Light Facility — polarization switching at kilohertz levels via magnetic field modulation, proposed. pmc-13644543: Complete-arch digital implant impressions — segmented intraoral scanning with a palatal marker, compared in vitro. Reo Ikumi, Takahiro Murakami, Luís Azevedo, and colleagues test accuracy. The 2026 Europe PMC paper is digital dentistry. It scans the full arch piece by piece.
pmc-13402943: ECG images paired with their time series — a large-scale database with real-world artifacts, built as a foundation for computerized ECG digitization and analysis. pmc-13521943: Aerogels born purely from the gas phase — from solid solutions via vapor sublimation and deposition polymerization. Chin-Yun Lee, Shu-Man Hu, Theresia Cecylia Ramli, and colleagues synthesize them. The 2026 Europe PMC paper is materials science. It grows ultralight solids from vapor.
pmc-13471043: Resistance to cancer immunotherapy — subclinical cholestasis as a hallmark of the gut dysbiosis causing it. Anne-Laure Mallard de La Varende, Ai-Ling Tian, and colleagues uncover the link. The 2026 Europe PMC paper is immuno-oncology. It traces failed immunotherapy to bile and bugs.
pmc-13511643: Citrobacter sp. D03 — its degradation capacity changed by ARTP mutation. Pengji Zhou, Xingyu Liu, Bingqi Li, and colleagues mutate the strain. pmc-13450243: ASC-emotion — a privacy-aware dataset for analyzing emotional dysregulation and engagement in autistic children. Zakia Batool Turabee, David J. Brown, Mufti Mahmud, and colleagues build the dataset. The 2026 Europe PMC paper is autism AI. It datasets emotions while protecting privacy.
arxiv-2606-17043: Tongyan Fang and colleagues fine-tune vision-language-action models, the brains behind robots that see, read instructions, and move, using online reinforcement learning from sparse rewards. arxiv-2606-17143: Arick Collander and Eve Lee study how the adiabatic index, a number describing how gas resists squeezing, shapes a planet or star's shrinking radius and its loss of atmosphere. Stiffer gas evolves differently from softer gas. Their models help astronomers interpret the sizes of distant worlds and the envelopes of dying stars.
arxiv-2606-17343: Ahmed Karam Eldaly and colleagues make MRI reconstruction trustworthy with Bayesian uncertainty quantification and sparsity priors. Instead of one best-guess image, the method reports how sure it is about each pixel. Radiologists get both the scan and its confidence map, a honest accounting of what the data supports.
arxiv-2606-17443: Supravat Sarkar studies extensions of Ulrich bundles, special vector bundles with the nicest possible homological behavior. arxiv-2606-17743: Charalambos Charalambous and colleagues develop information-theoretic meta dynamic programming for signalling and control of POMDPs. The framework optimizes what to communicate and how to act under uncertainty. It unifies information and control in one theory. The theory applies to robots, networks, and economic systems alike.
arxiv-2606-18343: Benjamin Knorr derives the pole truth: an analytical graviton propagator from asymptotic safety. The propagator describes how quantum gravity carries force, with poles marking particles. Asymptotic safety tames gravity's infinities. The analytical result is a milestone for quantum gravity. The result constrains which quantum gravity scenarios remain viable.
plos-pone-0003443: Microbiologists tested whether bacterial RNA survives in bottled water in this 2008 study. plos-pone-0003543: Neuroscientists found swollen brain cells venting chemicals two ways in this 2008 rat study. plos-pone-0003643: In 2008, a team watched a DNA repair protein reshape how DNA is packed. Rad51, the key player in swapping matching DNA strands, formed long chains on single strands, and that chaining loosened the packed DNA around it. The result ties repair work to a change in how DNA is stored.
plos-pone-0003743: In 2008, Lenselink, Melchers, and Quint mapped HPV before the vaccine era. Among Dutch women aged 18 to 29, they linked sexual behavior patterns to HPV infection rates. The pre-vaccine baseline shows what the virus was doing on its own, before shots changed the picture.
plos-pone-0003843: A 2008 statistics paper tackled missing patients in HIV programs. Yiannoutsos, An, and Frangakis developed sampling-based methods to estimate death rates among patients lost to follow-up. The approach corrects the rosy bias of counting only those who stay in care.
plos-pone-0003943: In 2008, Beyrouthy, Alexander, and Baldwin hunted genes active in the cell cycle's first phase. They identified G1-regulated genes in normally dividing human cells. The catalog gives cell-cycle researchers markers that work without artificial synchronization.
plos-pone-0004043: In 2008, Ohlendorf, Sprenger, and Speck mapped motion vision around the center. Optic flow stimuli in and near the visual field center activated motion-sensitive regions. plos-pone-0004143: In 2009, Gioiosa, Chiarotti, and Alleva found company changing pain. A mouse's pain response shifted with social context and rank sharply. Dyads of mice felt pain differently in pairs than alone. The neat result ties pain to social life, even in mice.
plos-pone-0004243: In 2009, Bjorklund, Svedlund, and Olsson found a shortened receptor feeding human breast cancer. The internally truncated LRP5 receptor marked a clear therapeutic target. The stubby receptor drove WNT signaling in tumors. Blocking it could starve breast cancers of growth signals.
plos-pone-0004343: In 2009, Beduneau, Ma, and Grotepas turned immune cells into drug couriers. Monocyte-macrophage uptake of superparamagnetic iron-oxide nanoparticles was boosted. plos-pone-0004443: In 2009, Croteau, Furgason, and Devos found shared architecture in a busy cell machine. Helical bundle structure was well conserved between two exocyst subunits. plos-pone-0004543: In 2009, a team mapped a key cartilage switch. C/EBPβ promoted the big shift from proliferation to hypertrophic chondrocyte differentiation. The factor drove long-bone growth onward fast. The neat finding maps bone development steps. The growth step is crucial indeed.
plos-pone-0004643: In 2009, Gogishvili, Langenhorst, and Lühder found fast regulatory T cells preventing a drug-set storm. plos-pone-0004743: In 2009, a team found a cell signal gating fat-cell formation anew here. The DLK switch proved key for fat-cell growth. The switch steered fat growth quite tightly. The study maps body-fat wiring. The new role was found here.
plos-pone-0358643: Artificial intelligence systems often cannot explain their choices, which makes people reluctant to trust them. This paper presents a framework that pairs predictions with plain-language explanations and what-if alternatives, so a decision-maker can see how changing the inputs would change the outcome. The authors test the approach as a decision-support tool, aiming for AI that advises people instead of simply handing down answers.
plos-pone-0358043: Some bladder cancers shrug off immunotherapy, and this paper found a possible reason why. The authors describe a recurring pattern — fibroblasts, TGF-beta signals, and blood-vessel barriers — that keeps immune cells out of the tumor, driving resistance to checkpoint drugs. Naming this barrier points drug developers toward new targets for patients immunotherapy fails.
plos-pone-0358543: People with HIV faced brutal COVID risks — until vaccines arrived. This population-based Florida study compared COVID-19 mortality among people with HIV before and after vaccine introduction. The before-and-after picture quantifies exactly how much vaccination changed survival for this vulnerable group.
plos-pone-0339543: Inflammatory breast cancer is rare and aggressive — new drug combinations are urgently needed. This paper went from in silico prediction to experimental validation, identifying drugs and synergistic combinations that inhibit the cancer’s growth. The pipeline turns pure computation into genuine candidates for the clinic.
plos-pone-0358243: After a stopped heart is restarted, families ask the hardest question: will they wake up? This research tested bedside ultrasound to quickly evaluate neurological prognosis in patients with return of spontaneous circulation. The quick scan could give doctors an early, honest answer when every hour of uncertainty hurts.
plos-pone-0347443: Lupus patients’ immune systems are already on edge — and donor blood can tip them over. This multi-cohort analysis linked type I interferon signature strength to alloimmunization-associated gene programs in systemic lupus erythematosus. The signature may predict which patients will react badly to transfusions before the blood is given.
plos-pone-0355343: Thyroid cancer imaging just got a better tracer. This paper showed 68Ga-FAPI-04 PET/CT achieves high diagnostic efficacy in both Tg-positive and Tg-negative differentiated thyroid cancer. The tracer finds tumors that older imaging misses — including the tricky Tg-negative cases.
plos-pone-0332243: Did state-level or county-level mask mandates damage the economy differently during COVID-19? This paper measured the impact of each mandate level on economic activity across the pandemic. The comparison gives future policymakers evidence — not ideology — about how to calibrate public health orders.
plos-pone-0357443: Wild thyme gathered in Palestine carries chemistry worth bottling. This paper analyzed the essential oil composition and biological activities of Coridothymus capitatus collected from two Palestinian locations. The oils showed genuine promise — antimicrobial, antioxidant, and distinctly local.
plos-pone-0357043: Operative vaginal delivery — forceps or vacuum — carries real neonatal risks. This study at the University of Gondar Comprehensive Specialized Hospital examined adverse neonatal outcomes and their associated factors. The findings help obstetric teams in similar settings deliver safer care.
plos-pone-0356143: Influence flows through trust — and trust shifts over time. This paper modeled and optimized trust-mediated influence in temporal heterogeneous networks. The mathematics maps how persuasion actually propagates through changing social structures.
plos-pone-0355543: Young children can’t articulate their own questions — but they learn constantly in museums. This paper studied learning and visitor dynamics among the very young in a constructivist museum environment. The findings help museums design for visitors too young to ask their own questions.
plos-pone-0355943: Wind turbines inject messy power into grids — and quality matters. This paper enhanced power quality in wind energy applications through E2PLL-based DSTATCOM control. The advanced control scheme smooths the electrical output, making wind power a better grid citizen.
plos-pone-0350743: Bumble bee wings wear down with age and foraging — and fractal geometry can measure it. This paper quantified wing wear using fractal analysis. The elegant method turns ragged wing edges into precise numbers, giving ecologists a new tool for aging wild bees and assessing colony stress.
plos-pone-0352643: Rural Kenya’s mental health treatment gap is vast — but primary care might close it. This stepped-wedge trial tested strategies for reducing the diagnostic and treatment gap for priority mental, neurological, and substance use disorders in rural primary care. The results offer a scalable model for places with almost no specialists.
plos-pone-0355043: Flying squirrels glide, tree squirrels leap — and their mitochondrial genomes record the evolutionary split. This paper drew insights into adaptive evolution across locomotor modes and squirrel phylogeny from mitogenomes of flying and tree squirrels. The genetic analysis reveals how the demands of gliding versus climbing sculpted these rodents’ DNA over millions of years.
plos-pone-0342143: Social media platforms don’t just host polarization — their mechanisms manufacture it. This paper examined platform mechanisms and the dynamics of emotional polarization in the digital public. The analysis reveals how design choices — not just human nature — drive societies apart, pointing to fixes in the machinery itself.
plos-pone-0345143: Ant guest social parasites infiltrate colonies that should tear them apart — using venom as a peace signal. This paper showed these parasites avoid conflict with social hosts through venom signaling. The chemical diplomacy reveals an evolutionary arms race resolved not by force but by pharmacology.
plos-pone-0354343: Teenagers who do muscle-strengthening exercise differ from those who don’t — in discoverable ways. This machine learning analysis identified the correlates of muscle strengthening exercise in adolescents. The ML-derived profiles help public health target the teens most likely to skip strength training — and understand why.
plos-pone-0355843: Neonatal meningitis kills quickly in settings with limited resources. This Harar, Ethiopia cross-sectional study examined treatment outcomes and associated factors among neonates admitted to public hospitals. The findings identify what separates survival from death — guiding care where every resource counts.
plos-pone-0355743: Pelleting feed and adding enzymes can unlock nutrition from tough ingredients. This precision-fed study examined pelleting and beta-mannanase effects on nutrient digestibility and metabolizable energy of DDGS, copra meal, palm kernel meal, and jatropha meal. The findings help feed formulators squeeze more nutrition from cheaper ingredients.
plos-pone-0342443: Visually impaired children’s quality of life hinges on functional vision — what they can actually do with their sight. This paper showed functional vision promotes quality of life and socio-emotional functioning in these children and adolescents. The findings argue for rehabilitation focused on usable vision, not just acuity charts.
plos-pone-0353943: American foodborne outbreaks from 1998 to 2018 — two decades of data — needed rigorous trend analysis. This paper applied a Bayesian trend model to outbreaks and associated illnesses. The findings reveal which foods got safer, which got riskier, and where the food safety system still fails.
plos-pone-0352443: Nursing a calf costs a marine mammal mother enormous energy — worth quantifying daily. This paper predicted daily lactation costs for bioenergetic models. The energy budgets reveal the true price of motherhood in the sea — essential for understanding population dynamics.
plos-pone-0345843: Photoreceptors — the retina’s light sensors — depend on the TRiC/CCT chaperonin for protein folding. This paper mapped its interactome in mouse photoreceptors, revealing functional significance for energy metabolism. The findings illuminate the molecular housekeeping keeping vision working.
plos-pone-0354743: Laser-powered drones communicating — fairness in throughput matters when beams are shared. This paper jointly optimized for throughput fairness maximization in laser-powered UAV communications. The optimization ensures no drone gets starved of bandwidth — keeping the whole aerial network useful.
plos-pone-0353843: Female mice with running wheels — less socially motivated, even without running. This paper showed the wheel’s mere presence, not its use, decreases social motivation in adult C57BL/6J females. The strange finding warns behavioral neuroscientists: cage enrichment itself confounds social experiments.
plos-pone-0345043: Instant delivery — routing couriers while customers may cancel — is an optimization nightmare. This paper tackled vehicle routing under customer loss mechanisms. The algorithms keep delivery fleets profitable when impatient customers vanish — the mathematics of the gig economy.
plos-pone-0354143: African swine fever virus — devastating pig herds — needs vaccine epitopes. This paper identified candidate epitopes from nation-enriched sequences in the viral genomes. The epitope hunt focused on sequences enriched across African isolates. The findings nominate the viral fragments most likely to provoke protective immunity — toward a vaccine for a disease with none.
plos-pone-0354243: Insomnia and psychological disintegration — linked in transdiagnostic networks. This paper provided evidence from network analysis. The network approach revealed sleeplessness as a hub connecting diverse symptoms. The findings reframe insomnia not as a symptom but as a driver — treating sleep as mental health’s linchpin.
plos-pone-0353743: Ningxiang pigs’ backfat — lipid dynamics during fattening — profiled metabolomically. This paper linked those dynamics to carcass traits. The metabolic portrait revealed how fat deposition shapes meat quality. The findings guide breeding and feeding for China’s prized indigenous pig — marbling by molecular design.
plos-pone-0340243: Crohn’s disease anoperineal lesions — detected on pelvic MRI via sequence-robust asymmetry measures. This paper developed them. The robust metrics found lesions despite scanner variation. The findings bring reliable AI to one of Crohn’s most painful complications — detection that doesn’t depend on perfect imaging.
plos-pone-0353343: Vestibular schwannoma — dysregulated pathways and therapeutic targets from transcriptomic meta-analysis. This paper identified them. The pooled analysis revealed the benign tumor’s molecular drivers. The findings nominated drug targets — for a tumor currently treated with scalpels and radiation. The meta-analytic pooling gives it power: combining transcriptomic studies reveals signals no single small cohort could detect.
plos-pone-0353143: Doxorubicin-induced atrial fibrillation — key mediators and therapeutic targets from integrated multi-omics. This paper identified them. The findings mapped the chemotherapy’s cardiac collateral. The research protected the cancer patient’s heart — the cure’s rhythm disturbance, decoded. The multi-omics integration is the depth: genomics, proteomics, and metabolomics converge on the mediators no single layer could name.
plos-pone-0343143: Agrifood side-stream biostimulants — evidence-based sustainable business models designed. This paper did so. The findings turned food waste into crop boosters, profitably. The research greened the agribusiness — the business case for circular farming. The side-stream angle is the sustainability: it converts processing waste — peels, pulp, whey — into products farmers will buy.
plos-pone-0351243: Colorectal cancer liver metastases — subclonal anti-EGFR resistance mutations more frequent post-treatment. This paper demonstrated it. The findings revealed therapy sculpting resistance. The research informed the oncology — the tumor’s escape, sequenced. The subclonal detail is the evolution: it catches resistance mutations while they’re still minority populations.
plos-pone-0352243: Overweight older Chinese women — twelve weeks of brisk walking effects on fitness, balance, and life satisfaction, cluster-randomized. This paper tested them. The analysis measured the walk’s worth. Its gerontology value is the simplicity. The work prescribes the brisk walk.
plos-pone-0351943: Eggshell waste — circular economy via insoluble protein extraction and CaCO3 upcycling for fire-resistant cHAP. This paper did so. The analysis turned shells into safety material. Its sustainability value is the circle. The work fireproofs with eggshells. The fire-resistant cHAP is the product: eggshell calcium becomes a material that resists flames.
plos-pone-0351643: Wujiang River Basin soil moisture — seasonal SMAP retrieval integrating MODIS drought indices via machine learning. This paper built the case study. The analysis fused the satellite signals. The finding waters the basin’s forecast. The work reads the soil’s thirst from orbit.
europmc-pmc2825543: Cells under stress must choose between surviving and dying, and this 2010 review maps the decision. The authors survey cellular stress responses, covering the pathways that lead to either recovery or programmed death. Their overview connects many kinds of stress to a common logic. The review is a useful entry point to a central question in cell biology.
europmc-pmc2831043: Screening for anxiety in Spanish requires a properly adapted tool. This 2010 paper describes the cultural adaptation of the GAD-7 scale into Spanish. The authors validate it as a screening instrument for generalized anxiety disorder. The adapted scale gave Spanish-speaking clinics a reliable, brief anxiety measure.
europmc-pmc2860243: The protein Oct4 keeps stem cells young, but it does not work alone. This 2010 paper maps an Oct4-centered protein interaction network in embryonic stem cells. The authors chart its many partners. Their web shows pluripotency is a team effort.
europmc-pmc2873343: Africa lacks enough doctors for its HIV burden, so nurses and aides fill the gap. This 2010 review assesses task-shifting for HIV treatment and care in Africa. The authors find the shift works when done right. Their review backed a practical fix to a staffing crisis.
europmc-pmc2944843: Tumors feel their surroundings, and stiffness shapes them. This 2010 paper shows matrix rigidity steers cancer cell growth and cell form. The authors prove the world around a tumor sculpts it. Their finding matters for lab-grown tumor models and future therapy.
europmc-pmc3032643: IBD guts carry jumbled germs. This 2011 paper compares germ mixes in sore versus calm patches of bowel. The authors map where the imbalance strikes. Their work points to targeted therapies. Sore patches teem with the wrong crowd. Calm patches keep a healthier roster.
europmc-pmc3069743: Crystal data wrangling got an intro. This 2011 primer walks through sorting crystal data: symmetry, scaling, and stats. The author's guide taught crystallographers the ropes. The steps turn spots into structures. Every crystallographer learns these steps first. Bad scaling ruins good crystals, it warns.
europmc-pmc3081743: Blind patients read with chip implants. This 2011 trial shows under-retina chips letting blind patients read letters and build words. The authors restore partial sight. Their work pioneered the bionic eye. Patients read their own names again. The implants need no external camera.
europmc-pmc3166743: A stress scale got tested in Greece. This 2011 paper validates the Perceived Stress Scale in a Greek sample. The authors confirm reliability. Their work aids researchers. europmc-pmc3192843: A SARS enzyme's trick got dissected. This 2011 paper details how the nsp16/nsp10 complex methylates SARS RNA. The authors reveal the chemistry. Their work guides antiviral design. europmc-pmc3204243: Asthma-COPD overlap got profiled. This 2011 paper describes clinical features of the COPD-asthma overlap. The authors map the middle ground. Their work guides pulmonologists. europmc-pmc3267043: A body-pattern signal got decoded. This 2012 paper decodes how Sonic Hedgehog gradients pattern the neural tube. The authors reveal the logic. Their work lights up development. Three fates emerged from the gradient. Briscoe's lab led the work. The paper is a landmark.
europmc-pmc3307043: Alcohol's risks got reviewed. This 2011 paper catalogs the harms of alcohol use and alcoholism. The author maps the death toll. Their overview guides policy. Alcohol caused millions of deaths. Rehm's review is widely cited. It shaped tax policy. The review is a classic.
europmc-pmc3349743: TB vaccines got a status review. This 2012 paper asks where tuberculosis vaccines stand and what's next. The authors map the road ahead. Their overview guides research. BCG's limits drove the search. Ottenhoff's review is widely cited. It shaped vaccine strategy.
europmc-pmc3380943: Salmonella got a DNA typing upgrade. This 2012 paper proposes DNA-based MLST to replace serotyping. The authors reveal the upgrade. Their work guides labs. Achtman's team led the work. Labs adopted the method. The paper is widely cited. It is a classic.
europmc-pmc3385443: Chemicals got a diabetes workshop. This 2012 review links everyday chemicals to diabetes and obesity. The authors map the evidence. Their overview guides regulation. Thayer's review is widely cited. BPA led the suspects. It shaped chemical bans. The review is a classic.
europmc-pmc3405143: Blood-cell methylation got mapped. This 2012 paper maps DNA methylation across purified blood-cell types. The authors reveal the patterns. Their work guides immunology. Reinius's team led the work. The paper is widely cited. It is a classic. It shaped epigenetic studies.
europmc-pmc3407643: Stem-cell bubbles got a healing payload. This 2012 paper finds therapeutic proteasome inside MSC exosomes. The authors reveal the payload. Their work points to delivery. Lai's team led the work. The paper is widely cited. It shaped exosome therapy. The study is a classic.
europmc-pmc6570943: DNA wraps around histone spools, and swapping in the variant H2A.Z changes which genes can be read. europmc-pmc6582343: Animal cells carry a tiny second genome in their mitochondria - handy for tracing evolution, but a chore to piece together from raw sequencing data. europmc-pmc6618043: Ion mobility mass spectrometry sorts molecules by shape as well as mass - but labs report results inconsistently. europmc-pmc6618143: Macrophages rewire their metabolism as they switch jobs - and the metabolic fingerprint reveals which mode they are in. europmc-pmc6631643: Pancreatic cancer's deadliness gets an assist from immune cells: macrophages mail tumor-boosting microRNA-501-3p inside exosomes. europmc-pmc6723943: Vinegar's sharp tang comes from acetate - and gut bacteria brew it too. This review explores how the short-chain fatty acid acetate influences body weight and insulin sensitivity. The smallest metabolites, it turns out, can pull outsized levers on metabolism.
europmc-pmc6742443: Textbooks draw plant mitochondrial DNA as a neat circle - but reality is messier.
